item.title: Co. Roscommon school in danger of closing due to low numbers
item.description: A school in County Roscommon could be forced to close due to low student numbers. Slatta National School near Rooskey has set a deadline of February 6th to preserve its two-teacher status. The Board of Management says it must enrol another ten students before then in order to keep the doors open. The school currently has eight students enrolled with three set to move on to secondary education next year. item.title: Longford TD says he plans to meet Ballymore CEO over Athlone plans
item.description: A Longford-Westmeath TD says he plans to meet with developer Sean Mulryan over plans for a 'Green City' in Athlone. Fine Gael's Parliamentary Chair Micheál Carrigy says he supports the ambitious project. Mr Mulryan and the Ballymore Group met with Roscommon councillors on Monday to discuss the plan. It would involve the population of the midlands town increasing to 100,000 by 2040. Deputy Carrigy says the development of a green city would benefit the entire region: Advertisement

item.title: Roscommon Cllr calls for more resources to be allocated to tackle littering
item.description: A Roscommon Councillor has called for more resources to be allocated to tackle littering in the county. Fianna Fáil's Paschal Fitzmaurice raised concerns about littering in Castlerea at a Muncipal District meeting last week. He says the current litter situation in the town leaves pressure on volunteers. Cllr Fitzmaurice also says funding that was set aside in a previous budget to tackle the issue still hasn't been used: Advertisement

item.title: Tributes paid to Co. Roscommon man following tragic incident in the UK
item.description: Tributes are being paid to a Co. Roscommon British Army Officer following a tragic accident at an army training site last weekend. Captain Philip Gilbert Muldowney died following a live firing incident in Northumberland on Sunday. The 25 year old grew up in the Ballinameen area of Co. Roscommon. Local Councillor Valerie Byrne says her thoughts are with the Muldowney family: Advertisement

item.title: Oireachtas members meet with Lough Funshinagh Flood Crisis Committee
item.description: Roscommon-Galway's four Oireachtas members have pledged to bring the ongoing flood crisis at Lough Funshinagh to the floor of the Dáil and Seanad on a monthly basis. The commitment comes as residents continue to face high water levels that threaten homes, farms, and local infrastructure. item.title: Glennon Brothers acquire UK timber processing business
item.description: A Co. Longford company has acquired UK timber processing business Pontrilas Group. Glennon Brothers is also timber processing business and is currently the main sponsor of Longford GAA and Pearse Park. Pontrilas is the largest timber processing mill in England and Wales and currently has a team of over 530 people. It also has a turnover of around 120 million pounds.
